front.title: Key-Value (KV) Cache Storage Protocol (KVSP): Indexing, Placement, Prefetch, and Migration for Distributed Inference

abstract.t: Large language model inference keeps the attention key-value (KV) cache of processed tokens so that they are not recomputed. When inference instances, cache tiers, and schedulers are separate components, possibly from different implementers, they need a common way to name reusable KV cache blocks, find where copies reside, protect copies from eviction while they are being loaded, steer work to the instance where loading is cheapest, and move a session to another instance after a failure. This document specifies the KV Cache Storage Protocol (KVSP), an HTTP-based protocol that defines a compatibility descriptor, keyed block identifiers that bind a block to its entire token prefix, a self-describing block container, a replica index with layer-granular residency, instance status reporting, leased prefetch directives, session checkpoints for migration, and a resharding procedure that retains sequence shards in place when a parallel group is resized.
